title: Build a community-run X / Twitter presence
summary: Help shape PearOS's voice and a community editorial process. Start with a proposal; the owner approves the account, contributors and posts before anything goes public.
steps: Read the project homepage and download the proposal template below. No coding is needed.
Suggest an account name, a short bio, community guidelines and a simple process for reviewing posts.
Draft five example posts and a one-week content plan in a document. Keep drafts private until reviewed.
Open the prefilled task conversation and introduce yourself. Share your proposal or a document link; wait for the owner to confirm scope, assignment and the exact reward.
After approval, help the owner set up the account using delegated access where supported. Submit the drafts for review before publishing.
acceptanceCriteria: A clear voice, bio and community conduct policy match PearOS's identity.
Five draft posts and a one-week plan include a named owner approval step before publication.
The handoff explains how community members suggest posts and how access is granted and removed.
No posts promise returns or imply Apple, Robinhood or platform endorsement.
deliverables: One proposal document with account/bio suggestions and editorial guidelines.
Five draft posts and a one-week content plan.
An owner-approved setup and handoff checklist.
approvalNote: Do not register an official account, post as PearOS or share account passwords before owner approval. Rewards and any paid assignment must be confirmed before paid work begins.

title: Build a welcoming PearOS Discord
summary: Design a friendly home for introductions, project updates and contribution help. The owner reviews the plan, server permissions and moderation approach before opening it to the community.
steps: Download the proposal template and sketch a small channel list: welcome, announcements, general chat and contribution help.
Write a welcome message, rules and a short guide for joining a task. A document or screenshots are enough; no code is needed.
Propose member/moderator roles, permission settings and a simple moderation process.
Open the prefilled task conversation, introduce yourself and attach your plan. Wait for the owner to confirm assignment, scope and the exact reward.
After approval, configure an owner-controlled server and test access with a normal member account. Ask the owner to review it before publishing an invite.
acceptanceCriteria: A small channel structure, welcome message and contribution guide are clear to a first-time visitor.
Announcements are restricted to approved maintainers; moderator permissions follow the reviewed plan.
Rules and moderation guidance cover spam, impersonation and unsolicited wallet/account requests.
The owner controls the server and approves the permissions, bot choices and public invite.
deliverables: A channel/role plan plus welcome text, rules and moderation guidance.
Screenshots or a checklist showing normal-member permission tests after approved setup.
An owner-approved handoff and invitation checklist.
approvalNote: Do not publish an official invite, install paid bots or grant administrator access before owner approval. Rewards and any paid assignment must be confirmed before paid work begins.
